results.note: Sweeping every one of the eleven Owner-only capabilities with an ordinary user context yields zero grants and eleven typed refusals, including the four AC-006 names explicitly — Codex, Workspace, Shell and the tool surface. The Owner-only and ordinary sets do not overlap, a suspended user reaches nothing at all across both sets, a context claiming the owner role is still resolved against the stored row, and the tool host runs its Owner guard before it resolves a tool.

The DEK is 32 random bytes per user — two users never share a wrapped key and the same user re-wrapped twice never produces the same ciphertext, so it is random rather than derived. It is wrapped with AES-256-GCM under a master-KEK-derived wrapping key, with the user scope in the AAD: another user presenting the envelope, or the right user with the wrong master key, both fail. The provider sub-key is derived by HKDF and bound to the provider and key version, so a different provider or a rotated version derives a different leaf and cannot read the record. Only the last four characters are ever stored in the clear. Reading the raw database file and its WAL after storing a credential finds no plaintext. Rotation re-wraps and preserves the credential; crypto-shred is final. Error paths carry a fixed message and a shape-only diagnostic, never the credential or the response body, and the Status surface refuses credential-shaped values.

The default count of inferred sensitive attributes is zero while ordinary facts still project. A sensitive attribute is refused as an inference at every confidence from 0.01 to 1 — the refusal precedes any confidence test, so there is no threshold at which it becomes allowed. Consent is per category: consent for one sensitive category does not unlock another, and consent only ever permits an explicit user statement, never an inference.

All three sources are pinned to exact 40-character commits with their modifications recorded and no temporary fetch remote retained. The AGPL text itself is kept, alongside third-party notices and upstream provenance. No runtime source clones, installs or fetches an upstream. Every declared dependency is pinned, caret-ranged against a lockfile, or vendored in the repository. One real licence discrepancy exists and is resolved rather than hidden: whereabouts-mcp declares AGPL-3.0-only in its package metadata while shipping a plain GPL-3.0 licence file; this node read the vendored file directly to confirm the lock is accurate, and the lock applies the combined expression GPL-3.0-only AND AGPL-3.0-only. The credential scan over the whole tree finds zero shapes in shipped code, docs or evidence; every match in the test tree is a declared synthetic vector.
